yearNews.text: Sensor kits get cheaper; community networks light up.
Battery packs for clinics drop in price again.
Local 3D print shops take municipal contracts.
Autonomy pilots expand on fixed routes.
Gene sequencing vans become almost routine.
Specialized quantum cloud jobs open for research partners.
Alternative proteins hit cafeteria budgets in pilot cities.
Long-horizon quantum links leave the lab in limited trials.

foresight.text: Utility-scale solar and wind are already among the cheapest new electricity sources in much of the world when paired with storage.
Battery pack costs have fallen for over a decade, enabling local microgrids and evening power.
Prediction: dense solid-state and next-gen packs further cut cost and fire risk this decade — still uncertain on exact year.
AI copilots and assistive models are already in clinics, schools, and logistics software worldwide.
Inference is moving to the edge; smaller models get cheaper to run locally and offline.
Prediction: clinical brain–computer interfaces expand from pilot trials to routine speech/motor restoration for narrow patient groups.
Medical and inspection drone corridors already operate in several countries for blood, vaccines, and infrastructure checks.
Autonomy expands first on fixed routes and mapped sites, then into messier open environments.
Prediction: driverless shuttles on geofenced corridors become normal in some cities before fully open-road robotaxis everywhere.
Pathogen sequencing during outbreaks and early gene therapies are real clinical tools, not only lab demos.
Time from sample to sequence continues to shrink; AI helps interpret results for non-specialists.
Prediction: alternative proteins reach price parity in more markets — adoption still depends on culture, regulation, and energy costs.
Cities and utilities already deploy sensor networks for floods, leaks, air quality, and grid stress.
Sensing gets cheaper; the hard part is governance — who owns the data and who acts on alerts.
Prediction: useful quantum applications stay narrow (materials, optimization niches) before general-purpose quantum networking.
Additive manufacturing already produces tools, spare parts, and some medical devices at local workshops.
Design files travel as bits; local fabrication capacity spreads as materials and printers improve.
Prediction: denser Earth-observation and connectivity constellations make near-real-time local environmental data routine for small towns.
Nuclear and geothermal already supply firm low-carbon power in regions that built them; new advanced designs are still ramping.
Interest in firm clean power rises wherever grids hit renewable intermittency walls.
Prediction: marine energy stays site-limited; winners are harbors and islands with strong resources and patient capital.
Milestone: climate attribution science and local flood/heat early-warning systems are already used by cities.
Trend: electrification of transport and cooking continues where grids and wallets allow — uneven by district.
Prediction: places that share sensors and response funds across jurisdictions will outpace those that wait for national programs.
Milestone: genomic surveillance and telemedicine expanded rapidly after recent pandemics, then stalled where funding and trust failed.
Trend: hybrid human+AI teaching and training spreads first where teachers and workers are scarcest.
Prediction: modular shelter + digital identity systems scale in crises only if local legitimacy and funding are solved first.

computing.name: Computing
computing.learn: Substrate for AI, networks, and software systems.
computing.inventionHint: Run models and coordinate local systems.
computing.scarcity: What scarce capability could Computing help make more abundant here?
computing.primer: Computing is the substrate under almost every modern system: processors, memory, software, and simulation. Local inventions often need somewhere to run models, store records, or coordinate devices — even offline at the edge. Capability is abundant in the cloud; the hard local problem is access, energy, skills, and who controls the stack.

maturity.now: Cloud and edge compute, commodity GPUs/CPUs, and software platforms that scale from phones to data centers.
maturity.near: Cheaper inference everywhere and tighter real-time local control loops for clinics, grids, and logistics.
maturity.frontier: Ambient compute so cheap and ubiquitous that energy and cost almost drop out of design constraints.

milestones: On-device AI chips in phones and industrial controllers
Widespread cloud regions and open-source software stacks
useCasesNow: Simulation for flood or traffic planning

energy.name: Energy
energy.summary: Physical power for work, heat, light, and industry.
energy.learn: How we generate and store energy shapes every other scale-up.
energy.scarcity: What scarce capability could Energy help make more abundant here?
energy.primer: Energy is the ability to do physical work — light, heat, motion, cold chain. Every local invention that pumps water, runs a clinic at night, or moves goods sits on an energy budget. The challenge is rarely “is electricity invented?”; it is reliability, cost, cleanliness, and who gets cut off first when the grid fails.

maturity.now: Mixed grids; diesel backup still common where reliability is poor.
maturity.near: More firm clean options and smarter demand response at community scale.
maturity.frontier: Energy scarcity largely exits everyday local design constraints.

milestones: Record renewable build-out in many markets
Falling costs for generation paired with smarter grids
useCasesNow: Hybrid backup that cuts diesel hours
energy.narrative: Power is the backbone of every fix.

crypto.name: Crypto-Currency
crypto.summary: Shared ledgers, tokens, and programmable incentives.
crypto.learn: Coordination and verification tools — with real scam risk.
crypto.inventionHint: Transparent local funds or supply proofs.
crypto.scarcity: What scarce capability could Crypto-Currency help make more abundant here?
crypto.primer: Crypto-currency and shared ledgers are tools for recording agreements, transfers, and proofs without a single trusted intermediary. Used well, they can make local funds transparent or track supply chains; used badly, they enable scams and volatility. For local inventing, think coordination and verification — not get-rich speculation.

maturity.now: Public ledgers, stablecoins, and pilot public-good funds; UX and fraud remain hard.
maturity.near: Clearer regulation and identity rails for procurement and aid.
maturity.frontier: Programmable money as boring default infrastructure for municipal finance.

milestones: Tokenized aid and supply-proof pilots in several jurisdictions
useCasesNow: Shared savings pools with public rules
crypto.narrative: Shared records settle local agreements in the open.

quantum.name: Quantum Computing
quantum.summary: Quantum processors for hard simulation and optimization.
quantum.learn: Early useful niches; not a laptop replacement.
quantum.inventionHint: Hard local optimization / research partner (later years).
quantum.scarcity: What scarce capability could Quantum Computing help make more abundant here?
quantum.primer: Quantum computing uses quantum effects for certain hard calculations — materials, chemistry, some optimization — that classical machines struggle with. It is not a faster laptop for city hall. Honest local use today is research partnership, learning, and long-horizon planning, not “quantum runs the clinic.”

maturity.now: Research machines and cloud access for experiments; not general IT replacement.
maturity.near: Niche hybrid quantum–classical jobs (materials, optimization pilots).
maturity.frontier: Broad practical quantum advantage in everyday municipal systems.

milestones: Cloud quantum access and improving error-mitigation research
quantum.narrative: Specialized quantum jobs open new designs.

geothermal.name: Geothermal Power
geothermal.summary: Heat from the Earth for steady power.
geothermal.scarcity: What scarce capability could Geothermal Power help make more abundant here?
geothermal.primer: Geothermal draws heat from the Earth for steady electricity or district heat. Where geology works, it is firm, low-carbon power. Where it does not, drilling and siting costs dominate. Invent with local resource maps and long capital horizons, not universal geothermal everywhere.

maturity.now: Proven baseload where geology is good; drilling cost and siting dominate.
maturity.near: Enhanced geothermal expanding viable sites.
maturity.frontier: Cheap firm geothermal nearly everywhere.

milestones: New enhanced geothermal pilots
Expanded district heat projects

tidal.name: Tidal Power
tidal.inventionHint: Coastal baseload where tides run strong.
tidal.scarcity: What scarce capability could Tidal Power help make more abundant here?
tidal.primer: Tidal power converts predictable tidal flows into electricity. Resource is site-specific and capital-heavy, but the predictability is valuable for islands and harbors. Invent only where tides and environment allow — and pair with storage and grid planning.

maturity.now: A few commercial sites; capital cost and marine impact still high.
maturity.near: More predictable coastal projects with better turbines.
maturity.frontier: Cheap tidal power for any coast.

milestones: Operational tidal arrays in select strong-current channels

solar.name: Solar Power
solar.learn: Fastest-scaling clean generation when paired with storage.
solar.scarcity: What scarce capability could Solar Power help make more abundant here?
solar.primer: Solar photovoltaic turns sunlight into electricity — now among the cheapest new generation options in much of the world when sites and policy allow. Night and cloudy reliability need storage or backup. Local inventing thrives on roofs, pumps, clinics, and microgrids with honest battery pairing.

maturity.now: Cheap PV for roofs, clinics, pumps; storage needed for night and reliability.
maturity.near: Even cheaper packs and integrated microgrids.
maturity.frontier: Energy abundance limited mostly by land and politics.

milestones: PV among cheapest new generation in much of the world
solar.narrative: Roofs drink sunlight for local work.

wind.name: Wind Power
wind.scarcity: What scarce capability could Wind Power help make more abundant here?
wind.primer: Wind power converts wind into electricity at utility or community scale. It is mature but intermittent and politically local (siting, wildlife, views). Pair with storage, demand flexibility, or firm power for clinics and industry that cannot wait for the wind.

maturity.now: Mature onshore/offshore turbines; siting and grid flexibility are the fights.
maturity.near: Better storage pairing and community ownership models.
maturity.frontier: Wind plus storage as default cheap power with little friction.

milestones: Record capacity additions
Long multi-year cost declines in many markets
wind.narrative: Turbines stitch power into the landscape.

wave.name: Wave Power
wave.scarcity: What scarce capability could Wave Power help make more abundant here?
wave.primer: Wave power harvests energy from ocean swells. Potential is large; surviving storms and hitting cost targets remains hard. Invent as harbor or island pilots with patient capital — not as a universal coastal default this decade.

maturity.now: Mostly pilots; storm survival and cost still hard.
maturity.near: Harbor-scale arrays with better reliability.
maturity.frontier: Cheap wave power along any energetic coast.

milestones: Multi-year pilot arrays surviving harsh sea states

nuclear.name: Nuclear Power
nuclear.learn: High capacity; trust and cost dominate.
nuclear.inventionHint: Regional firm power for industry and desal.
nuclear.scarcity: What scarce capability could Nuclear Power help make more abundant here?
nuclear.primer: Nuclear fission offers dense, firm low-carbon power. Large plants and emerging small modular reactors face cost, trust, waste, and schedule challenges. Local inventing is usually regional planning and industrial heat partnership — not a backyard reactor for one ward.

maturity.now: Large plants and some SMRs under construction or early operation; trust and cost dominate.
maturity.near: More SMR deployments and factory-built modules.
maturity.frontier: Plug-and-play firm nuclear for every city that wants it.

milestones: First commercial SMR projects
Life-extension of existing fleets
nuclear.narrative: Firm clean power anchors the region.

battery.name: Battery Technology
battery.summary: Storing electricity for mobility and grids.
battery.learn: The partner that makes solar and wind local-real.
battery.scarcity: What scarce capability could Battery Technology help make more abundant here?
battery.primer: Batteries store electricity for later — evening clinic lights, EV fleets, solar firming. They make intermittent renewables local and useful. Chemistries improve; mining, fire safety, and recycling remain design constraints. Invent for real kilowatt-hours and duty cycles, not infinite free storage.

maturity.now: Li-ion packs for EVs and home/clinic storage; density and cost still improving.
maturity.near: Safer denser chemistries more common at local scale.
maturity.frontier: Storage ceases to be the bottleneck for most local renewables.

milestones: Multi-year cost declines enabling home and grid storage pilots
battery.narrative: Power waits in packs until needed.

ai.name: Artificial Intelligence
ai.summary: Systems that predict, recommend, generate, and decide from data.
ai.learn: Automates pattern-finding; still needs human accountability.
ai.scarcity: What scarce capability could Artificial Intelligence help make more abundant here?
ai.primer: Artificial intelligence finds patterns in data to predict, recommend, generate text or images, and support decisions. It is already a co-worker in many clinics, classrooms, and logistics desks — but it can be biased, overconfident, or opaque. Strong local inventions keep humans accountable and scope the model to a real workflow.

maturity.now: Assistive models, classification, forecasting, and copilots with human oversight.
maturity.near: More reliable agents for narrow workflows; better local-language models.
maturity.frontier: Broad autonomous judgment in high-stakes domains without humans — not honest for most missions yet.

milestones: Generative AI copilots in work, education, and some clinical tools
ai.narrative: Local assistants draft routes and lessons.

robots.name: Robots
robots.summary: Machines that sense, move, build, care, or inspect.
robots.learn: Physical automation — bodies for intelligent software.
robots.scarcity: What scarce capability could Robots help make more abundant here?
robots.primer: Robots are machines that sense and act in the physical world — carrying, inspecting, assisting care, or rebuilding. Software intelligence needs a body to move goods or people. Today’s wins are often supervised, mapped environments; open-world autonomy is still the stretch.

maturity.now: Warehouse, inspection, and limited care/assist robots under supervision.
maturity.near: More reliable mobile manipulators in mapped indoor sites.
maturity.frontier: General household robots that handle any chore unsupervised.

milestones: Hospital logistics robots and industrial cobots in daily use
robots.narrative: Machines share work; people keep judgment.

networks.name: Networks
networks.summary: Moving information and coordination across distance.
networks.learn: The rails that let other tools reach people.
networks.scarcity: What scarce capability could Networks help make more abundant here?
networks.primer: Networks move information and coordination across distance — fiber, cellular, mesh, satellite. Without them, sensors cannot alert, telemedicine cannot reach, and AI cannot sync. Local inventing often means last-mile connectivity, resilience in outages, and who is still excluded.

maturity.now: Cellular, fiber, mesh, and satellite links; coverage gaps remain intensely local.
maturity.near: Cheaper community meshes and resilient failover for clinics and schools.
maturity.frontier: Universal high-quality connectivity as default everywhere.

milestones: LEO satellite broadband and community mesh pilots expanding access
networks.narrative: Links stitch distant rooms into one response.

transportation.name: Transportation
transportation.summary: Moving people, goods, and medicine physically.
transportation.learn: Access is often a logistics problem.
transportation.scarcity: What scarce capability could Transportation help make more abundant here?
transportation.primer: Transportation is how people, goods, and medicine move physically. Many “tech” crises are logistics crises: the vaccine, the midwife, the spare part is hours away. Invent for corridors, last mile, and reliability under weather and poverty — not only vehicles that look futuristic.

maturity.now: Buses, bikes, vans, ferries, and logistics software already move care and goods.
maturity.near: Better demand-responsive transit and EV fleets on fixed corridors.
maturity.frontier: Frictionless zero-emission mobility for every trip with no planning.

milestones: EV buses and optimized routing cutting cost on many urban routes
transportation.narrative: Goods and care arrive with less waste.

self-driving.name: Self-Driving Cars
self-driving.summary: Vehicles that navigate with limited human control.
self-driving.learn: Slow safety deployment; huge local mobility stakes.
self-driving.inventionHint: Shuttles, freight corridors, access for non-drivers.
self-driving.scarcity: What scarce capability could Self-Driving Cars help make more abundant here?
self-driving.primer: Self-driving vehicles aim to navigate with little or no human control. Progress is real in geofenced areas and advanced driver assistance, but open-road reliability, edge cases, and liability still limit scale. Local inventing often means shuttles and freight on mapped routes, not “all traffic is autonomous tomorrow.”

maturity.now: Geofenced robotaxi/shuttle pilots and ADAS; full open-road autonomy limited.
maturity.near: Fixed-route shuttles and freight corridors more common.
maturity.frontier: Universal driverless mobility in any weather and road.

milestones: Commercial robotaxi zones
Autonomous shuttles on mapped routes

drones.name: Drones
drones.summary: Uncrewed aircraft for delivery, sensing, response.
drones.learn: Already flying medical and inspection routes in places.
drones.scarcity: What scarce capability could Drones help make more abundant here?
drones.primer: Drones are uncrewed aircraft for delivery, inspection, mapping, and search. Medical corridors already save time for blood and vaccines in several countries. Urban free-flight swarms are still constrained by airspace, noise, and safety rules — invent with corridors and missions, not unrestricted sky.

maturity.now: Mapped corridors for medical delivery, inspection, and mapping in many countries.
maturity.near: Denser urban operations with clearer regulation.
maturity.frontier: Fully free-roaming swarms as default logistics.

milestones: Operational medical drone corridors for blood and vaccines
drones.narrative: Small craft deliver and watch overhead.

quantum-internet.name: Quantum Internet
quantum-internet.summary: Networking quantum states for secure links.
quantum-internet.inventionHint: Ultra-secure links for critical local nodes (late game).
quantum-internet.scarcity: What scarce capability could Quantum Internet help make more abundant here?
quantum-internet.primer: Quantum internet aims to network quantum states for ultra-secure links and distributed quantum tasks. It is early research infrastructure, not a city ISP replacement. Local inventing may mean pilot secure links between critical sites with research partners — not entanglement for every household.

maturity.now: Lab and metro testbeds; not commodity city infrastructure.
maturity.near: Limited secure links between specialized sites.
maturity.frontier: Routine entanglement networking across regions.

milestones: Quantum key distribution and network experiments in research corridors
quantum-internet.narrative: Quiet secure links join critical sites.

space.name: Space Exploration
space.summary: Orbit and beyond for observation, comms, defense.
space.learn: Satellites already shape weather and connectivity.
space.inventionHint: Local use of orbital data and links.
space.scarcity: What scarce capability could Space Exploration help make more abundant here?
space.primer: Space systems — especially satellites — already deliver weather, imaging, and connectivity that towns use on the ground. Local inventing is about using orbital data and links for flood maps, crop stress, or backhaul — not building a launch pad in the mission place.

maturity.now: Earth observation, weather, and connectivity constellations already local-relevant.
maturity.near: Cheaper revisit times and more direct-to-device links.
maturity.frontier: Instant global sensing and connectivity with no gaps.

milestones: Dense LEO constellations for broadband and frequent imaging
space.narrative: Orbital eyes and relays serve the town.

synbio.name: Synthetic Biology
synbio.summary: Designing living systems as tools and factories.
synbio.scarcity: What scarce capability could Synthetic Biology help make more abundant here?
synbio.primer: Synthetic biology designs living systems — microbes, cells, genetic circuits — as tools for medicines, materials, diagnostics, and environmental work. It is a broad family, not one product. Much is tightly regulated; invent with partnerships, labs, and guardrails, not “programmable life runs the city” as if it were a mobile app.

maturity.now: Sequencing, some gene therapies, industrial enzymes, regulated biotech products.
maturity.near: Broader biomanufacturing access; more agri and clinical apps under regulation.
maturity.frontier: Programmable living systems as everyday municipal infrastructure.

milestones: Pathogen genomics in outbreaks
Approved gene therapies for select diseases
synbio.narrative: Living tools enter the local toolkit.

bci.name: Brain-Computer Interface
bci.summary: Direct links between neural signals and machines.
bci.learn: Clinical restoration first; broader use later.
bci.inventionHint: Restore speech or movement for specific patients.
bci.scarcity: What scarce capability could Brain-Computer Interface help make more abundant here?
bci.primer: Brain–computer interfaces translate neural signals into computer commands or stimulation — restoring communication or movement for people with severe disability in clinical settings. Consumer mind-apps are mostly hype for local missions. Invent with clinical pathways and consent, not mass surveillance of thoughts.

maturity.now: Clinical and research interfaces for severe paralysis and communication restoration.
maturity.near: Broader clinical speech and motor prostheses.
maturity.frontier: Consumer high-bandwidth brain apps as normal interfaces.

milestones: Trial participants communicating via advanced BCIs

genetic-engineering.name: Genetic Engineering
genetic-engineering.summary: Changing genomes for traits and therapies.
genetic-engineering.inventionHint: Local health or crop resilience tools.
genetic-engineering.scarcity: What scarce capability could Genetic Engineering help make more abundant here?
genetic-engineering.primer: Genetic engineering changes genomes for crops, therapies, or industrial microbes under regulation and ethics debates. Local inventing may mean resilience crops or clinical pathways with institutions — not open DIY editing of ecosystems.

maturity.now: Engineered crops, select gene therapies, industrial microbes under regulation.
maturity.near: More therapies and climate-resilient crops with governance fights.
maturity.frontier: Open local genome editing as everyday DIY infrastructure.

milestones: Approved CRISPR therapies
Widely planted engineered crops in some regions
genetic-engineering.narrative: Careful genetic tools enter clinics and fields.

gene-sequencing.name: Gene Sequencing
gene-sequencing.scarcity: What scarce capability could Gene Sequencing help make more abundant here?
gene-sequencing.primer: Gene sequencing reads DNA/RNA to identify pathogens, risks, and sometimes guide care. Outbreak vans and wastewater surveillance already exist. Invent for speed-to-action and privacy — a sequence without response is only a file.

maturity.now: Portable and lab sequencers map pathogens and clinical panels routinely in capable systems.
maturity.near: Faster bedside panels and lower-cost whole genomes.
maturity.frontier: Instant full biological readout for any sample by anyone.

milestones: Outbreak sequencing vans
Wastewater genomic surveillance
gene-sequencing.narrative: Genomes become readable maps for action.

alt-proteins.name: Alternative Proteins
alt-proteins.learn: Lower land and emissions intensity of protein.
alt-proteins.inventionHint: Local protein when supply chains break.
alt-proteins.scarcity: What scarce capability could Alternative Proteins help make more abundant here?
alt-proteins.primer: Alternative proteins — plant, fermentation, cultivated — aim to deliver nutrition with less land and emissions intensity. Culture, cost, and energy still gate adoption. Invent for school and clinic menus or local fermentation, not overnight replacement of every diet.

maturity.now: Plant and fermentation proteins on shelves; cultivated meat mostly pilot/early market.
maturity.near: Price parity in more categories; clearer labeling and energy costs.
maturity.frontier: Default protein with negligible land and animal use everywhere.

milestones: Supermarket plant/fermentation proteins
Limited cultivated-meat approvals
alt-proteins.narrative: Protein is produced closer to plates.

vr.name: Virtual Reality
vr.summary: Immersive training and remote presence (VR/AR family).
vr.learn: Practice and shared seeing without full travel.
vr.inventionHint: Train skills, rehearse disasters, remote expertise.
vr.scarcity: What scarce capability could Virtual Reality help make more abundant here?
vr.primer: Virtual and augmented reality create immersive or overlaid views for training, remote expertise, and rehearsal of high-risk work. They do not replace roads or clinics, but they can multiply scarce experts and let people practice before real storms or surgeries. Accessibility and motion sickness still limit who benefits.

maturity.now: VR/AR training, remote expert overlays, and simulation for high-risk skills.
maturity.near: Lighter headsets and better multi-user local training rooms.
maturity.frontier: Full sensory presence that replaces most physical co-location.

milestones: Surgical and disaster training and remote-assist AR in hospitals and utilities

print3d.name: 3D Printing
print3d.summary: Turning digital designs into physical objects on-site.
print3d.learn: Local manufacturing of parts, tools, shelters.
print3d.inventionHint: Print what you cannot wait to ship.
print3d.scarcity: What scarce capability could 3D Printing help make more abundant here?
print3d.primer: 3D printing turns digital designs into physical parts on-site — tools, braces, fixtures, sometimes medical devices. It shortens supply chains when ships and trucks fail, but quality control, materials, and certification still matter. Invent for urgent local fabrication with clear SOPs, not magic printers of everything.

maturity.now: Local fabs print tools, spare parts, and some medical devices under quality limits.
maturity.near: Broader certified materials and municipal print hubs.
maturity.frontier: Any object on demand from digital files with perfect strength.

milestones: Workshop and hospital makerspaces producing spare parts under SOPs

iot.name: Internet of Things
iot.summary: Sensors that make the physical world measurable.
iot.learn: See floods, air, machines, bodies — then act.
iot.scarcity: What scarce capability could Internet of Things help make more abundant here?
iot.primer: The Internet of Things is sensors and actuators that make the physical world measurable and sometimes controllable — flood height, cold-chain temperature, air quality, machine vibration. The hardware is often cheap; the hard parts are power, maintenance, false alarms, privacy, and who acts on the data.

maturity.now: Cheap sensors for water, air, and assets; networks and maintenance are the bottleneck.
maturity.near: Denser meshes with better battery life and analytics.
maturity.frontier: Invisible continuous sensing of entire districts with perfect action loops.

milestones: City flood, air, and water sensor networks in production use
iot.narrative: The place reports its own stress.

materials.name: Material Science
materials.summary: New solids and surfaces — strength, filters, conductors.
materials.scarcity: What scarce capability could Material Science help make more abundant here?
materials.primer: Material science designs solids and surfaces — strength, filtration, insulation, conductivity. Better materials make flood barriers, lighter rebuilds, cleaner water, and better batteries possible. Invent for what the place must withstand, with recycling and toxicity in the story.

maturity.now: Advanced composites, membranes, and coatings in industrial supply chains.
maturity.near: Cheaper high-performance materials for local builders.
maturity.frontier: Self-healing programmable materials as default building stock.

milestones: Commercial membranes
Lighter structures
Better thermal materials
materials.narrative: Surfaces adapt to weather and wear.

nano.name: Nano-Technology
nano.summary: Engineering at nanometer scale for medicine and materials.
nano.scarcity: What scarce capability could Nano-Technology help make more abundant here?
nano.primer: Nanotechnology engineers matter at nanometer scale for drug delivery, sensors, and coatings. Regulated products already exist; general nanofactories do not. Invent with safety data and dual-use caution — especially for medical or environmental release.

maturity.now: Nanomedicine delivery, coatings, and sensors in regulated products.
maturity.near: Broader clinical and filtration uses with clearer safety data.
maturity.frontier: General-purpose nanofactories in every clinic.

milestones: Approved nanomedicine formulations
Commercial nano-coatings
nano.narrative: Tiny layers clean and deliver carefully.

portside-floods.title: Portside Ward floods again
portside-floods.scene: The school gym is the emergency shelter for the third time this decade. Fishers lose weeks of work when the quay goes under. Residents want something that works *here*, not a national slogan.

saline-well.title: The well turned saline
saline-well.scene: One town’s main well is brackish. Tanker prices spike every dry month. Kids miss school to haul water. A fix must be affordable and maintainable locally.

border-fever.title: Fever cluster at the border clinic
border-fever.scene: A small clinic sees a new fever pattern among travelers. Staff are three nurses deep. They need detection, logistics, and trust — this week, not after a conference.

three-schools.title: One science teacher, three schools
three-schools.scene: Three rural schools share one science teacher who drives 90 minutes between them. Labs are empty half the week. Students who can leave, leave.
three-schools.stakeholder: Ms. Reyes, the shared science teacher

arrival-city.title: Four thousand arrivals, one winter
arrival-city.scene: A mid-size city expects 4,000 new arrivals before spring. Gyms are full. Paperwork is chaos. Locals fear queues at clinics. Dignity has a deadline.

warehouse-shifts.title: The night shift disappeared
warehouse-shifts.scene: Warehouse automation cut 30% of shifts in eighteen months. Rent didn’t fall. Workers want retraining that leads to real pay — not a pamphlet.

opaque-benefits.title: The benefits AI nobody can question
opaque-benefits.scene: City hall wants to deploy an opaque AI to decide benefits *this year* and cut costs. Caseworkers are already overruled by a black box pilot. Prevention means a better system, not a ban on tools.

smog-corridor.title: School days lost to smog
smog-corridor.scene: Asthma days close classrooms along the truck route. Parents have sensor photos of the haze — and the corridor still runs diesel at rush hour. A local fix must protect kids and cut corridor exhaust.

dark-clinic.title: The clinic dies at dusk
dark-clinic.scene: When the grid fails, vaccines warm and night births go dark. Diesel is expensive and late. Staff need first watts that stay on.

empty-nets.title: Empty nets, angry quay
empty-nets.scene: Fish stocks collapsed locally. Some boats still cheat night limits. Young people leave. Monitoring and alternatives have to work for this harbor.

memory-house.title: Who watches the watchers of memory
memory-house.scene: A day center for people with dementia has a waitlist of fourteen months. Families burn out. Staff need tools that preserve dignity — not just surveillance.

maternal-road.title: Two hours to the next theater
maternal-road.scene: Complications mean a two-hour road trip if the rains haven’t washed the bridge. Midwives want backup that arrives in time.

shelter-winter.title: Winter count keeps rising
shelter-winter.scene: Encampments grow under the overpass each winter. Hotels are full. Building codes move slowly. People need warm, safe options *this* season and a path to stay housed.

food-desert.title: The last greengrocer closed
food-desert.scene: A dense neighborhood’s last fresh-food shop closed. Corner stores sell calories, not vegetables. Transit to a supermarket is two buses.

five-coasts.title: Five coasts, no shared warning
five-coasts.scene: Five small coastal towns share a storm path but not a budget or data pipe. Each mayor waits for the other to buy sensors. Coordination *is* the invention.

cancer-wait.title: Scan wait times hit nine months
cancer-wait.scene: Imaging backlog means late diagnoses. Rural patients miss appointments. Oncologists want triage and tools that find risk earlier without inventing a miracle drug overnight.
